> ## 🧭 STANDING ORDER (set 2026-08-02 by the comrade, after the frontier survey)
> **Prioritise the UNTOUCHED realms over deepening the ones we already hold.**
> A realm at 92% gives back single subtests; a realm at 0.8% gives back hundreds —
> and, more to the point, the untouched ones are the ones a real page *needs to
> function*. When a session's ⭐ points deeper into a realm already above ~85%, and
> an untouched realm below ~40% is on the survey, **take the untouched one** and
> leave the ⭐ written down for later. Say in the scroll that you did, and why.

Playwright's injected script compiles the caller's function with `eval`, **inside the page**; a real browser runs it in an **isolated world** that carries no policy. That looks pointlessly strict until you notice why — sanitising markup removes the dangerous parts and leaves a document, and **there is no equivalent for a program**. The only useful thing a policy can say about code is *"yes, exactly this, I have seen it"*, and the identity check is how the platform makes it say so rather than guess. It also throws **`EvalError`**, not the `TypeError` every other sink throws, so a page's existing `catch` keeps working when it turns Trusted Types on. ⭐ **And a policy delivered in a HEADER is the same policy**: Trusted Types shipped with its own tiny directive reader that walks `<meta>` and nothing else, so a site sending `require-trusted-types-for 'script'` **the ordinary way** got no enforcement at all. *Two implementations of one thing is a bug waiting for a delivery path.* **⛔ Cap: `trusted-types` name-list enforcement, and `require-trusted-types-for` in a report-only policy, are still inert.** |

## 🗺️ Captain's Counsel (recommended order — **re-surveyed 2026-08-02, quest #453**)

> The counsel below this box was written on **2026-06-14, session 5**, and was never
> revised while quests #100→#453 followed each other's ⭐ pointers deeper and deeper
> into CSS. It is kept for the record. **The live map is the measured one:**
> **[`102-the-frontier-survey.md`](102-the-frontier-survey.md)** — 152 files across
> **33 top-level realms the ledger had never touched**, each compared against Chrome
> on the same files.
>
> **The headline: we cover 21 of WPT's 262 top-level realms. Inside them we score
> 88–99%. Outside them we score 0–48% against a Chrome at 93–100%.**
>
> Recommended order, weighted by the mission rather than by subtest count:
> 1. **`fetch` (187/1204) + `streams` (77/585)** — the data layer of every modern
>    page. A page whose `fetch()` fails renders EMPTY. Largest winnable block on the map.
> 2. **`cookies` (0.8%) + `webstorage` (34.9%) + `IndexedDB` (2.9%)** — staying logged
>    in, and working offline, which matters most where connections are metered.
> 3. **`accname` (0.0%) + `wai-aria` (25.1%)** — accessible-name computation is how a
>    screen reader says what a button is **and how an AI agent identifies one**. We
>    score ZERO on the API that says what an element IS. Highest mission-value per
>    subtest on the map; `accname` is 3 files, 144 subtests, Chrome 98.6%.
> 4. **`pointerevents` (22.6%) + `uievents` (32.0%) + `selection` (6.0%)** — how the
>    agent acts, where (3) is how it reads.
> 5. **`quirks` (48.1%) + `css/CSS2` (79.5%)** — the old web, which is most of the web
>    on a hand-me-down laptop. `css/CSS2` is the closest to bankable on the map.
>
> **NOT yet:** `wasm` (191k subtests) and `editing` (108k) are the biggest by weight
> and the poorest by value — mechanical spec conformance and `contenteditable`.
>
> **Two findings that are not scores:** `resize-observer/eventloop.html` **HANGS the
> engine** hard enough to wedge the harness and require a server restart (a hang is
> worse than a wrong render — worth its own quest); and the entire **visual** half of
> the platform is still unmeasurable here, because `wpt_baseline.py` cannot run CSS
> reftests. A reftest runner is the campaign's largest instrumentation blind spot.

<details>
<summary>Superseded: the 2026-06-14 counsel (session 5)</summary>



With **#02 Attr-Node Codex SECURED (67/67)** — a real `Attr`/`NamedNodeMap` model
over namespace-aware Rust attribute storage — the field stands thus:

1. **The Collections Armory (11)** + **Node-Smithing Vaults (06)** — now the most
   leveraged ground: `getElementsByTagName(NS)` and the `Node-*` family are
   measurable and the new `Attr`/`NamedNodeMap`/namespace machinery directly
   supports them (`Element-getElementsByTagName` sits at 4/19 today).
2. **The Selector Sorcery (01)** — finish the tail (see Scroll 01 for the bucketed ~52):
   namespace selectors, shadow-DOM pseudo-elements, a real `NodeList` type, and a
   harness node-identity mystery. Namespaced attributes are now real, which helps.
3. **The ClassList Mutation-Echo (03)** (1315/1420) — bankable tail on held ground.
4. **The Iframe Frontier (12) tails** — `Range-insertNode`/`surroundContents`
   per-subtest correctness (909/698 of 1840). Grinding but bankable.
5. The smaller self-contained realms (08 Encoding, 09 FileAPI) for breadth.
6. **Standing leverage:** XML-document mode + iframes-delay-load (#05) and the new
   namespace-aware attribute layer (#02) may unblock OTHER XML/foreign-content tests.

## 📜 Lands already secured this campaign (for the chronicles)

**Session 2026-09-06 (Quests #605–#624 — the mathematical arc: twenty quests over an UNTOUCHED realm. Scroll [`491-the-mathematical-verdict.md`](491-the-mathematical-verdict.md)):**
**THERE WAS NO MATHML.** Not "MathML with gaps" — none. `is_mathml_element()` in the layout engine's selector glue returned `false` with the comment `// not implemented.....`; there was no MathML user-agent stylesheet in either the computed-style engine or the renderer; every `<mi>`, `<mfrac>` and `<mtable>` wrapped as `HTMLUnknownElement` and reported its tag name as `MI`/`MFRAC`/`MTABLE` — uppercased, which foreign content never is; and an `<mspace width="20px">` measured **0 × 0**. That last one is the whole realm: every MathML test in WPT loads `mathml/support/feature-detection.js`, and nearly every `has_<element>` in it resolves to **`has_mspace`**, which asks one question — is `<mspace width='20px'>` twenty pixels wider than a bare `<mspace>`? It was not, so 246 test files agreed among themselves that this browser has no MathML and stopped at their first assertion. A realm of 3407 subtests gated behind one box that did not exist.
**Chosen under the standing order** — `mathml` had **zero mentions in `WPT_PROGRESS.md`** after 604 quests, sat at 21.1% against a Chrome at ~99%, and is the realm a homework page is made of.
**#605 `MathMLElement`** — the interface existed as a bare class nothing was an instance of; MathML-namespace elements (parsed and `createElementNS`) now wrap as it, and it carries the `GlobalEventHandlers` mixin (`math-global-event-handlers` 75/375 → **375/375**).
**#606 ⭐⭐ Foreign content keeps its case.** The `tag_name` op ASCII-uppercased unconditionally, and `localName` was derived by lowercasing the result — so `<math>` was `MATH` and **SVG's `<foreignObject>` was `FOREIGNOBJECT` with a `localName` of `foreignobject`, engine-wide**. Now uppercased only for HTML-namespace elements in an HTML document, with the raw local read through a new op (memoised per wrapper).
**#607/#608/#609** the MathML Core UA stylesheet in the computed-style engine; the attribute mapping (`dir`/`mathcolor`/`mathbackground`/`mathsize` — 0/165 → **165/165**); `math-depth`/`math-style`/`math-shift` as real inherited properties with `scriptlevel`/`displaystyle`/`mathvariant` mapping onto them (33/132 → **132/132**).
**#610/#611 ⭐⭐⭐ THE GATE.** A MathML UA stylesheet in the renderer gives MathML elements boxes for the first time, and `<mspace>`'s `width`/`height`/`depth` — pure geometry with no content to size it — map to `width` and `height: calc(height + depth)` through the ordinary CSS declaration parser (which enforces MathML's own rule that a bare number is not a length). One box, and 246 files started running.
**#612** grammar for the three math properties, so `e.style.mathDepth = "invalid"` is refused and `add()`/`auto-add` resolve against the parent. **#613** `<mfrac>` stacks — but only when well-formed; any child count but two is invalid markup that lays out as a plain mrow.
**#614 ⭐⭐ MathML rows are FLEX containers, because whitespace between MathML elements is not content.** The space a human types between `<mn>1</mn>` and `<mo>+</mo>` is not rendered; inline layout turned it into a real space box and every spacing measurement in the realm came back one space-width too wide. Flex generates no anonymous item for whitespace-only text, and `align-items: baseline` is what an mrow does anyway. Token elements stay inline-block — their whitespace IS content. **#624** does the same for MathML in an *inline* formatting context (a `<mtd>`'s anonymous mrow).
**#615** `<msqrt>` draws a radical sign. **#616 ⭐⭐ operator spacing** — `lspace`/`rspace` as margins (outside the operator's own box), applied only when the parent uses **mrow layout**, and around the whole **embellished operator**: an `<mo>` wrapped in an `<mrow>` puts its space before the *mrow*, with the `<math>` root as the one place the hoisting stops (`no-spacing` 0/54 → **51/54**).
**#617** a MathML element with `display: contents` computes to `none` — a rule about the computed value no stylesheet of any origin can express.
**#618 ⭐⭐ `Selection.toString()` returns RENDERED text.** It was `Range.toString()`, which concatenates raw `data`; the Selection API asks for what the user sees, i.e. with `text-transform` applied — which is how MathML's automatic italic becomes observable: a single-character `<mi>` copies as its **italic mathematical alphanumeric symbol** (0/112 → **112/112**).
**#619 ⭐⭐⭐ css-logical properties had NEVER reached their physical counterparts.** `padding-block-start: 10px` computed `padding-top: 0px`; `margin-left: 7px` computed `margin-inline-start: 0px`; `inline-size` and `width` were strangers — on every element of every page. Both names now go to the cascade and the stronger declaration wins, mapped through the element's own computed `writing-mode`/`direction`. **Engine-wide, not MathML**: `css/css-logical` **17/269 → 167/269** over five files (A/B-proved by disabling the mapping and rebuilding), and it is what `force-horizontal-tb` (0/68 → **68/68**) was really asking for.
**#620 ⭐⭐ `font-size: math`** — the 0.71-per-level scaling that makes a superscript smaller than its base. Stylo compiles `math-depth`/`math-style`/`font-size: math` for **Gecko only**, so in this build they are not cascadable at all; the depth is derived structurally from the tree (every rule that sets it *is* structural) and emitted as a percentage font-size. Written twice on purpose — renderer and computed-style engine — so the box a page gets and the style it reads agree. **#621** an accent keeps its font size (`scriptlevel-001` 4/16 → **16/16**). **#622** under/over scripts stack.
**#623 ⭐⭐ "in-flow children" is a question about computed styles**, and there is exactly one place in this pipeline that can ask it: the presentational-hint pass runs before the children are styled, and layout-tree construction is undone by the Taffy-style rebuild that follows it. The child-count rules live in the style flush, immediately after that rebuild.
**Realm 719/3407 → 2850/3409**, 92 files up, **0 down**, 79 files at 100%. **Zero-regression ritual: 341 rows, 55226 → 55280 (+54)**; the two flagged rows both proven (`IndexedDB/keygenerator` re-proved 21/21 solo on the new binary; the documented flaky img file swings 226/184/215 on the BASE binary alone). ⚠️ The kill-by-name trap bit again — `pkill -f 'obscura serve'` does not match `obscura-base serve`, so the base server silently failed to bind and two "base" measurements were of the new binary; kill by port when two binaries are in play.
⛔ **Caps, named honestly:** this is an approximation, not MathML layout — no fraction bars, the radical is a character not a stretchy glyph construction, no font-MATH-table script shifts (~120 subtests across `displaystyle-*`, `frac-parameters-*`, `subsup-parameters-*`, `cramped-*` need test fonts with MATH tables); `display: math` does not parse in this stylo build; the operator dictionary (Appendix B) is unimplemented; embellished operators do not filter out-of-flow children; `contain: size` is unmodelled; the realm's other ~350 files are reftests (quest **F7**).
⭐ **And one thing this arc found and did NOT fix: `position: fixed` is not viewport-relative.** `stylo_taffy` maps `Position::Fixed` to Taffy's `Absolute`, so a fixed element is laid out against its ancestor chain — `left: 100px` lands at **108px** on a page with the default body margin. That is every sticky header, modal and toast on the web. **Top next-leverage.**

**Session 2026-08-18 (Quests #595–#604 — the named arc: ten quests. Scroll [`490-the-named-verdict.md`](490-the-named-verdict.md)):**
**#595 ⭐⭐⭐ THE WINDOW HAD NO PROTOTYPE CHAIN.** `Object.getPrototypeOf(window)` was `Object.prototype`; `window.constructor` was not `Window`; `Window.prototype` existed but nothing inherited from it — and with nowhere for a named-properties object to live, "named access on the Window object" was faked by eagerly defining an own getter on the global for every `id` present when parsing finished. That fake could not see an element added later, could never forget one that left the tree, ignored `name` entirely, and returned one element where the spec returns an `HTMLCollection`. Now `window → Window.prototype → WindowProperties` with HTML's real named-objects algorithm (child navigables by live TARGET NAME, `embed`/`form`/`img`/`object` by `name`, any element by `id`, HTMLCollection when several). Three traps: the lookup RECURSES into itself (a latch, raised *before* the liveness check, because `_windowIsLive` reads a missing property); a cross-origin frame throws on every internal read and poisoned every missing-property lookup on the window; and an `<iframe id=quux>` is reached as the ELEMENT, not its window.
**#596 ⭐ an index past the last frame is a NAME.** `window[0..63]` are own accessors, so they could never fall through to the named-properties object; `window[3]` with three frames returned undefined instead of the frame named "3". vs-named 3/10→**10/10**.
**#597 ⭐⭐ BarProp.** `window.locationbar` and its five siblings did not exist, so `support/window-open-popup-target.html` threw on its first line — the page behind all 51 rows of popup-behavior. Six DISTINCT objects per Window, stable for its lifetime; `visible` false once discarded and false for every bar of a popup.
**#598 ⭐⭐ `window.open` features decide popup-ness.** Full tokenization, HTML boolean-feature parsing, and "check if a popup window is requested" — a feature string asking for the full set of bars still gets a tab; dropping any one asks for a popup. ⚠️ `noopener`/`noreferrer` short-circuit to "tab" (not in the prose, but what browsers do and what all 51 rows assert). popup-behavior 0/51 TIMEOUT→**51/51**.
**#599 ⭐⭐ `noopener` does not mean "make a new window".** An existing target with that name is still reused, still navigated, and still keeps its opener; all `noopener` withholds is the RETURN VALUE. noopener?indexed 1/9→**9/9**.
**#600 ⭐ `document.referrer` existed nowhere** — `undefined` where the spec says `""`. Added on Document/DetachedDocument/_IframeDocument; an auxiliary window inherits its opener's URL, and `noreferrer` means no opener AND no referrer. noreferrer 0/1→**1/1**.
**#601 ⭐⭐ a navigated window kept the OLD Location.** `location`'s component fields were computed once at construction, so assigning `href` on navigation left `search`/`pathname`/`origin` describing the previous document — every reused popup that navigated to `target.html?channelName` read an empty `location.search` and opened `new BroadcastChannel("")`. This was the invisible half of #599: the window navigated and the page on the other end still could not be heard.
**#602 ⭐⭐ `object` and `embed` are browsing contexts.** `window.length` counted `iframe` only. A container is `iframe`/`frame` always, `object` while it has `data`, `embed` while it has `src` — and NOT when the type is a plugin/media type (an `<embed type=image/png>` is a picture; a whole subtest asserts such a document has zero child contexts). `embed` has no `contentWindow` in WebIDL, so the engine reaches a container's window internally. Losing the URL destroys the context as a QUEUED TASK, not synchronously. ibc-02 0/3→2/3, ibc-03 0/1→**1/1**.

**Session 2026-08-09 (Quests #530–#534 — the attested, unframed, owned & vouched arc: `integrity` was a string this browser reflected and never read, and a cross-origin frame's `location` was readable by anyone who framed it. `subresource-integrity` 33/48 → 48/48 — a whole realm, zero rows before; `frame-ancestors` non-nested files 4/11 → 14/14; `sandbox`+`inheritance` 41-file slice 7/100 → 10/100):**
Region chosen under the standing order: the CSP realm has 1,362 files and ~165 had ever been measured, so the *dark half* — `frame-ancestors`, `sandbox`, `inheritance`, `inside-worker`, `embedded-enforcement` — plus `subresource-integrity`, a whole realm at zero rows. Baselined first: **188/863 over 241 files** (`scripts/wpt-csp-dark-probe.txt`).
**#530 the attested verdict.** ⭐⭐⭐ **`integrity` was reflected and never read.** Every `<script integrity="sha384-…">` on every page loaded whatever the CDN sent, and the author believed otherwise — the thirteenth *feature that answers, and answers wrong*, giving the same wrong answer CSP used to give: *"yes, this is the file you asked for."* And it is the protection that matters most to the people this browser is for: a page on a metered connection leans hardest on shared CDNs, and hashing bytes that already arrived is free. ⭐⭐ **Only the strongest algorithm in the list counts and the weaker ones are not a fallback** — otherwise an attacker who can forge only sha256 appends a sha256 token and every integrity attribute on the web is worth its weakest entry. ⭐⭐ **An integrity check on an opaque response is not a check, it is an oracle** (hash a no-cors body and any page reads any cross-origin file one guess at a time) — which is why the answer is *blocked*, and why every correct `<script integrity>` carries `crossorigin` beside it. ⭐ The promise is snapshotted at *prepare a script*, not when the bytes land, or a page could disarm its own promise one statement after making it. ⭐ Wired at **three** seams — and the one that matters is Rust's markup `<script src>` path, because **almost every real `integrity` attribute on the web is in markup**.
**#531 the unframed verdict.** `frame-ancestors` and `X-Frame-Options` (which did not exist at all) — the only directive that is not about what a page may load but about **who may load the page**, and ⭐ **the one protection a site cannot enforce itself**: it must be honoured by the browser of a reader visiting somebody else's page. ⚠️⚠️ **THE FIND WAS OLDER THAN CSP: a cross-origin frame's `location` was readable.** `contentDocument` was guarded; `contentWindow` never was — so any page could embed any site and read where that frame ended up (session live? which account? which order?). ⚠️⚠️ **And the first fix was wrong in an instructive way: the opacity belongs to the HANDLE, not to the window.** One realm means the object the embedder gets from `contentWindow` *is* the object the framed page calls `window`; making that throw breaks the framed page, which is entitled to read its own URL and is usually the only code that does. Same shape as #521's isolated-world find — *when one realm must model two principals, the distinction lives in the reference.* ⚠️⚠️ **The embedder must hear nothing**: firing `securitypolicyviolation` at the parent (where a global report helper naturally puts it) is a reliable **framability oracle**, the exact question the directive exists to stop answering. ⭐ A source expression **with a path matches no ancestor at all**. ⭐ `frame-ancestors` overrides XFO **outright**, not "stricter wins", or the migration breaks.
**#532 the owned verdict.** ⭐⭐⭐ **A policy belongs to a document, not to a browser.** `_cspState.policies` was one global list for the whole realm — the top page's policy silently governed frames that never asked for it, and **a frame that sent a strict policy of its own ran completely unprotected.** Now a `WeakMap` per document, fed by the framed response's own headers and `<meta>`. ⭐⭐ **Local schemes inherit wholesale** — without that rule `<iframe srcdoc="<script>…">` is a one-line hole in every policy on the web and `createObjectURL` is the second one.
**#533 the owned verdict, second half: `<iframe sandbox>` DID NOT EXIST** (`grep -n sandbox` over the DOM returned three comments and no code). A restriction the page asked for and silently did not get is worse than one it never had, because the site embedded the thing *believing the box was closed*. ⭐ The `sandbox` attribute and the CSP `sandbox` directive merge as an **intersection of allowances** — a document may always ask for more restriction on itself, never less. ⚠️ **The flags had to settle at NAVIGATION, not in the script path**: computed where the scripts run, a frame that carries no code — an image, a PDF, a plain page — never gets its opaque origin, so the commonest use of the attribute would hold only for the frames that carried code.
**#534 the vouched-hash verdict** closed the cap #519 named, with the machinery #530 built: a CSP hash-source authorises an **external** script by matching its `integrity`, not its URL. ⭐ The rule is **every**, not any — a script pinned to two digests of which the policy lists one has not been fully vouched for. ⚠️ And a hash-source policy is a *comment* unless something verifies the response actually is those bytes; **the policy names the file, SRI proves it is that file**, which is why the two specs cross-reference each other instead of each growing a parser.
⛔ **The arc's honest cap, named by three directories at once: iframe documents share the page's realm.** The 22 nested `frame-ancestors` files, most of `sandbox/`, and 20 of 24 `inheritance/` files load a second `testharness.js` **inside a frame** and relay results by `postMessage`. That is not a CSP problem — the flat files prove the directives are right. ⚠️ Also: the `frame-ancestors` suite hard-codes `https://wpt.live:8443`, so on our default `:443` base every "same-origin" frame is cross-origin and the allow-cases fail for a non-engine reason (`url-allow` is **0/1 on `:443`, 1/1 on `:8443`, same binary**); the probe list carries `:8443` URLs with the reason written above them.

**Session 2026-08-09 (Quests #525–#529 — the incremented, unblocked, linked, sealed & fetched arc: the browser stopped rebuilding the whole page every time it was asked where something is. Mutate-then-measure 13.65 ms → 2.70 ms; `editing` 78183/80787 → 82256/83982; `input-events` 1805/2980 → 2119/3209; ZERO regressions over the 227-file ritual):**
Took the leverage list in order. **#1 had been named by THREE consecutive arcs** and it was time.
**#525 the incremented verdict.** Profiled first, and the profile decided the quest. Serializing the whole DOM on every query — the thing everyone assumes is the problem — costs **160 µs, one percent**. The cost was that each query threw the styled, laid-out document away and built an identical one. ⭐⭐⭐ **`blitz-dom` has an `incremental` Cargo feature and we had never enabled it** — it took a repeat resolve from 3.84 ms to 0.23 ms, and in doing so *proved the whole quest*: a live document with no damage is nearly free, so everything above it was the price of not keeping one. Then a **journal** in `DomTree` (taken at the tree's own mutation primitives — `with_node_mut` is the single door to every attribute and character-data write; `detach` catches every structural removal including the implicit unlinks) feeding **whole-element rewrites** into a persistent Blitz document via `DocumentMutator`. Blunt by design: the journal knows *which* element changed, never *how*, and rebuilding it from the page's own serialization is the one patch that cannot disagree with a re-parse. ⭐⭐⭐ **`DummyHtmlParserProvider::parse_inner_html` is an empty function body** — Blitz's default — so the first working build **silently emptied every element it patched**: no error, no return value, no log, just a `<div>` that came back 12 px tall (its border and padding, and nothing else). *A method that can silently do nothing is a method whose default must be checked.* ⭐⭐ The one real regression the ritual caught was a **genuine bug in the fork**: `final_layout.content_size` is only written by the layout paths that compute it, so an element that becomes **inline-level is measured rather than block-laid-out** and kept reporting the scrolling area it had as a block — *a `scrollWidth` from a layout that no longer existed.* Fixed where Blitz clears the Taffy cache: **clearing a cache is a promise the value will be recomputed, and any field only sometimes recomputed must be cleared there too.** Proof: a 19-step mutation script dumping every element's rect, `offset*`, `client*` and `scroll*` — patched and re-parsed dumps **identical, all 19 steps**. ⚠️ Harness trap that cost a cycle: `pkill -f 'obscura serve'` does not match `obscura-pre serve`, the new server died on `Address already in use`, and **`until curl :9222/json/version` passed against the OLD server** — *a readiness check any server can satisfy is not a readiness check.*
**#526 the unblocked verdict** collected the debt. No new code — the same files against a faster engine. `editing/run/delete.html?6001-7000` **0/1000 → 948/1000**, two could-not-run slices → 997/1000 and 981/1000, three more variant slices that had never been reached at all now scoring. ⭐ **Read the denominators**: `input-events` went 2,980 → **3,209 total subtests**, because a timeout does not report the tests it never got to. *A score whose denominator moves when you change nothing but speed was measuring the clock.* **A cap named honestly in a scroll is still a number missing from the scoreboard.**
**#527 the linked verdict.** `getComputedStyle` **did not see external stylesheets at all** — the cascade collected `querySelectorAll('style')` and nothing else, while LAYOUT went through Blitz, which fetches `<link>` files itself. ⭐⭐ **Two subsystems disagreeing about the same document is worse than either being wrong alone**: `getBoundingClientRect()` measured a styled page and `getComputedStyle()` described an unstyled one, and every framework that compares the two is built on that comparison. `body` background: `rgba(0,0,0,0)` → `rgb(255,255,255)`. The bytes were already arriving — `_loadElementResource` had `parsed.body` in hand and dropped it. Fetched **before the first script runs** (HTML's "style sheets that are blocking scripts"), because *a script that measures before its CSS has landed measures a page that never existed*. ⚠️ **The WPT yield is 3 subtests and the reason is worth writing down: WPT inlines its CSS** — a conformance suite puts its styles in a `<style>` block so the test is one self-contained file. **Do not let a probe's silence talk you out of a real bug.**
**#528 the sealed verdict** closed the fourth road #522 missed: a CSP-blocked `<style>`/`style=""` **still reached the renderer**. ⭐ The flag needed already existed — `emit_nids` is true for exactly one caller, the layout bridge, so it marks *the one serialization CSP gets a say in*; `innerHTML` keeps showing the page its own markup, because CSP stops a declaration applying, it does not edit the document. Also: a blocked attribute now yields an **EMPTY declaration block** (CSSOM builds it from what was *applied*), which closes last arc's shipped moved row — `inline-style-allowed-while-cloning-objects` 18/25 → **21/25**, above the 19/25 it held before #522. ⚠️ And it surfaced a latent bug in #525: **an empty patch list is not "nothing changed"** — the snapshot hash says something did and the journal could not account for it; taking it as proof of a match froze the box tree.
**#529 the fetched verdict** stopped `object-src`, `frame-src`, `worker-src`, `manifest-src` and `prefetch-src` failing open. One gate at the one place element resources go through, asked **before** the fetch — the request itself is the leak. ⭐⭐ **`new Worker` does not throw**: the check happens inside *fetch a classic worker script*, so a refusal is a network error and HTML fires `error` **at the Worker, asynchronously**. The version that threw looked obviously right and made the test **time out** — *a constructor that throws where the spec fires an event breaks every page that wrapped the call in a `try`/`catch` it never expected to reach, and its `onerror`, the code actually written for this, never runs.*

**Session 2026-08-09 (Quests #520–#524 — the varied, evaluated, cascaded, outbound & compiled arc: the eval hook that two realms had been waiting on, and the half of CSP that decides where the data GOES. 130-file CSP probe 154/325 → 181/322, 19 files improved; `trusted-types` compilation sinks 0/12 → 12/12):**
Took the outgoing knight's leverage list in order — #4 (the runner), #2 (the eval hook), #3 (more CSP) — and found that #2's stated solution did not exist and did not need to.
**#520 the varied verdict** taught `scripts/wpt_run.py` to expand `<meta name="variant">`. `wptrunner` — and wpt.fyi, and therefore every score we compare ourselves against — runs a variant file **once per variant**; we ran the bare URL once, and several suites end their variant switch with `throw new Error("Unhandled variant")`, so those files scored **0** for a reason with nothing to do with the engine. Quest #517 had worked around it by maintaining twelve query strings **by hand** in one probe list.
**#521 the evaluated verdict** closed the cap #519 named as its biggest single follow-up — and closed it the other way round. **The V8 hook is not reachable**: `rusty_v8` 137 binds only an on/off switch, which fires *before any JavaScript runs* (so no violation report could ever be sent, and every one of these tests asserts the report) and which would gag **the engine's own compilers** — inline `onclick=""` handlers, frame scripts, worker bodies, AudioWorklet processors, none of which `'unsafe-eval'` governs. ⭐⭐⭐ **And the objection to wrapping `eval` does not apply to a BLOCKED eval**: the direct-vs-indirect distinction only matters when the call actually runs code, and a blocked one never does — *so the engine gives up exactly nothing.* The wrapper installs **only when a policy has an opinion**, so the 99% of pages with no CSP keep the real `eval` with its real semantics, and it closes the `({}).constructor.constructor('…')()` door as well as the global binding. ⚠️⚠️ **THE FIND: THE AUTOMATION CHANNEL IS NOT THE PAGE.** The first working build made every CSP-protected page **completely unreadable** — not the test, *anything*: `page.evaluate("() => 1+1")` came back `undefined`. Playwright's injected script compiles the caller's function with `eval`, **inside the page**, and a real browser runs that code in an **isolated world** which shares the DOM and carries no policy of its own. Obscura has one realm and cannot isolate by construction, so the gate asks Rust instead (`runtime::PrivilegedScript`, an RAII guard around each CDP evaluation). **Without it, the browser locks itself out of exactly the sites that took security seriously** — precisely backwards, and a bug only a browser built to be driven could have found. ⚠️ Two cheap traps, both expensive: `const f = function eval(x){}` is a **SyntaxError in strict mode**, which took the whole bootstrap with it (a browser with no DOM) — and the panic was invisible because **`cargo build … | tail -3` reports tail's exit code, not cargo's**. Grep for `^error|panicked|Finished`, never pipe to `tail`.
**#522 the cascaded verdict** wired `style-src`, whose checker had existed since #519 with **nothing calling it** — so every `-blocked` test failed and every `-allowed` one passed for free. A stylesheet is not decoration: an attribute selector plus a `background-image` URL **exfiltrates a CSRF token one character at a time** with no JavaScript at all, and `style=""` is the injection that **survives every sanitizer that only strips `<script>`**. ⚠️ **A GATE IS ONLY A GATE IF EVERY ROAD GOES THROUGH IT** — the style attribute took three patches and each looked complete: skip the attribute source in the cascade (still applied, because **the live declaration block is seeded FROM the attribute** the first time anything touches `el.style`, which `getComputedStyle` itself can cause); skip that too (still applied, because `_specifiedDecl` has a **fallback that reads `el.style` directly, around the cascade**). One declaration, three doors. ⚠️ **`violatedDirective` IS `effectiveDirective`** — CSP3 keeps the older name as an alias of the same value, and reporting the *declared* directive instead looks more informative while making inline-`<style>` and `<link>` violations indistinguishable to any report consumer. ⚠️ **And the sweep must run before the page's first script**: lazily, the page has already made legal CSSOM writes that were reflected into the attribute, so the sweep reads them, cannot tell them from markup, and blocks the page's own styling. *A false positive is worse than a missed detection.*
**#523 the outbound verdict** did `connect-src`, `base-uri` and `form-action` — the three directives about **what leaves**, each closing a route that needs no script running at the moment it is used. One injected `<base href="//evil/">` re-points every relative URL on the page at once; one line rewriting a form's `action` sends the password to somebody else on a page that still looks exactly like the real one. ⭐ The value is in **what the failure looks like**: a blocked `fetch` **rejects** (it must not resolve with an error `Response` — a page that gets a Response back believes it reached the network), an async XHR fires **`error` on a task**, a sync one **throws** because there is no later task, `sendBeacon` returns **false**, and a blocked `<base>` is **ignored** rather than erroring. ⚠️ **A port is a number, not a string of digits**: `:080` and `:80` are the same port, and comparing spellings refuses a policy the spec itself calls a match.
**#524 the compiled verdict** is the "two realms, one hook" the outgoing knight promised, reached by a hook nobody expected: #521's own JavaScript-level gate. ⭐⭐ **The compilation sink is not like the others.** Every other Trusted Types sink accepts what the default policy hands back — that is how Trusted Types is meant to be adopted, one sink at a time. `eval` requires the policy's return value to be **string-identical to its input**. That looks pointlessly strict until you see why: sanitising markup removes the dangerous parts and leaves a document, and **there is no equivalent for a program** — the only useful thing a policy can say about code is *"yes, exactly this, I have seen it"*. ⭐ **And a policy delivered in a header is the same policy**: Trusted Types shipped with its own tiny directive reader that walks `<meta>` and nothing else, so a site sending `require-trusted-types-for 'script'` **the ordinary way** got no enforcement at all. *Two implementations of one thing is a bug waiting for a delivery path.*
**⚠️ ZERO REGRESSIONS, THE STRONG PROOF: the ritual list run against the PRE-ARC binary and the new one, diffed PER FILE — 230 rows, 0 could-not-run in both passes, 51,701 → 51,703, and the only two moved rows were IMPROVEMENTS** (`the-img-element/naturalWidth-…` 209 → 210, the file the memory already flags as flaky under batch load; `csp/script-src/script-src-1_1` 2/3 → 3/3). Each pass ~7 min at 5 shards / chunk 3. Note the row count: the list is 219 entries and produced **230 rows**, because #520's variant expansion turned several files into the several tests they always were.

One file in the CSP probe moved **19/25 → 18/25** (`inline-style-allowed-while-cloning-objects`) and is reported as a moved row rather than buried. External `<link>` stylesheets are still not in the JS cascade at all, and a blocked style still reaches **layout**. WebSocket is still ungated by `connect-src`; `frame-src`/`object-src`/`media-src`/`font-src`/`worker-src` still parse and fail open; redirect hops are unchecked.

**Session 2026-08-08 (Quests #517–#519 — the intended, declared & reported arc: TWO untouched realms opened. `input-events` 180/3,240 → 1,805/2,978 (17 files improved); `content-security-policy` 88/219 → 141/279 (26 files improved, could-not-run 19 → 3). ZERO regressions over a 211-file pre/post per-file ritual diff):**
Chose both regions under the **standing order** after baselining three untouched candidates side by side. `mathml` was surveyed and **deliberately passed over**: its `relations/html5-tree` files already score for free, and almost everything else in the realm is a **reftest**, which is quest F7's cap, not an engine gap — taking it would have bought layout work disguised as conformance work. The cheap `math-depth`/`math-style`/`math-shift` CSS properties are banked in writing instead.
**#517 the intended verdict** — `InputEvent` was a **complete, correct, fully-built interface that nothing in the entire browser ever dispatched**. Quest #516 taught this engine to edit; nothing told the page. Every rich editor written since about 2018 is a `beforeinput` listener over a contenteditable, and told nothing, they do nothing: the box takes focus, the caret blinks, and every keystroke vanishes. Worse — **a keystroke inside a `contenteditable` did nothing whatsoever**, because the UA half, the *default action* of a key inside an editing host, had never been written. ⭐⭐⭐ **THE FIND THAT WENT BEYOND THE TESTS: the CDP key path was doing its own, wrong, editing.** `Input.dispatchKeyEvent` appended typed text to the **end** of an `<input>`'s value and made Backspace chop the **last** character off, both ignoring the caret and any selection — so an agent driving Obscura to fill in a form typed at the end of the field no matter where the caret was, and every correction deleted the wrong character. It fired a bare `Event('input')` (so `e.inputType` was `undefined`), fired even when the page had `preventDefault()`ed the keydown, and did nothing at all in a contenteditable. All of it is now one implementation, so **a key means the same thing however it arrived**. ⭐⭐ **A focused editable box always has a caret, and ours did not** — `.focus()` left the document with no selection, and every editing command is defined over the selection, so the box had focus, looked ready, and refused every command in silence. ⚠️ And the fix had to go in the **right place**: putting the detached-node check inside `_edActiveRange` made the two largest files in the realm TIME OUT, because `isConnected` walks `parentNode` and **every hop is a round trip into the Rust DOM**. *A correctness fix in a hot path is a performance bug wearing a correctness fix's clothes.* ⭐⭐ **The target range of a deletion is not always a character** — it is a selection, or one code point, or **a block boundary with nothing inside it**, which is a merge. ⭐⭐ **Deleting the last character of a wrapper deletes the wrapper**, and the range has to grow **end first**, because the start's growth is measured against the grown end. ⭐⭐ **A selection is not always ONE target range**: drag across a `contenteditable="false"` widget and what is about to be deleted is the editable text on either side — two ranges with a hole — reported as `deleteContent`, *without a direction*. Also built: `DataTransfer`/`DataTransferItem`/`DataTransferItemList`, which the engine's own exposure table already claimed to have and had never defined, and real `cut`/`copy`/`paste` (closing a #498 cap).
**#518 the declared verdict** opened `content-security-policy` — 4,354 subtests, 1,362 files, zero ledger rows, and `grep -rn "content-security-policy" crates/ --include=*.rs` **returned nothing**. ⭐⭐⭐ **A CSP failure is invisible from BOTH sides**: the site sent the header and got a 200 and no report (no report arrives when nothing is blocked either); the reader sees a page that looks exactly like a protected one, until the day it doesn't. Twelfth *feature that answers, and answers wrong* — and the worst kind, because the wrong answer is **"yes, run it"**. It is also **free**: no download, no script, no frame of work, which is exactly the kind of protection that should reach a second-hand phone first. Landed: the policy/directive/source-expression parser, the fifteen-deep fallback chain, header **and** `<meta>` delivery, nonces, SHA-256/384/512 hashes, and the gates for inline `<script>` and inline event-handler attributes. ⭐⭐⭐ **A nonce or a hash in the list turns `'unsafe-inline'` OFF** — the apparent contradiction that lets one policy serve old browsers and new ones correctly. ⭐⭐ **A `<meta>` policy governs only what comes AFTER it, and that is a rule about TIME**: in a streaming parser it is automatic, but **this engine parses the whole document before running the first script**, so without an explicit document-order check a meta retroactively blocked the scripts above it. ⚠️⚠️ **`'self'` is a URL matcher even though it is quoted like a keyword** — skipping every quoted token skipped the most common source expression on the web, and **29 files flipped to could-not-run at once**; *a mass conversion to could-not-run is a load-bearing symptom, not noise*. ⚠️ And the markup-handler fallback was a hole: `_fireElementError` `eval`s an un-activated `onerror` attribute directly, so `script-src-attr` would have stopped every handler **except the one on the element that failed to load** — precisely the `<img src=x onerror=…>` payload it exists to stop.
**#519 the reported verdict** made it say so: `SecurityPolicyViolationEvent` with all twelve attributes, `report-uri` POSTing an `application/csp-report`, report-only as a real disposition distinct from enforcement, and enforcement for `img-src` and external `<script src>`. **Report-only is how CSP actually gets deployed** — nobody switches a strict policy on and hopes — so an engine that cannot report is one on which nobody can safely *adopt* CSP. ⭐ **A blocked image fires `error`, not silence**, because the whole point of an `onerror` fallback is to put something in the hole. ⭐ **A `*` wildcard does not cover `data:`** — those schemes carry their payload inside the URL. ⭐ **A nonce authorises an EXTERNAL script too**, which is why the gate needs the node id and not just the URL.
**⚠️ ZERO REGRESSIONS, THE STRONG PROOF: the 211-file ritual run against the PRE-ARC binary and the new one, diffed PER FILE — 210 of 211 rows identical, 0 could-not-run in both passes, and the single moved row was an IMPROVEMENT** (`the-img-element/naturalWidth-…` 179 → 188, the file the memory already flags as flaky under batch load). Each pass is ~6m40s at 5 shards.

**Session 2026-08-08 (Quests #514–#516 — the commanded, styled & typed arc: `editing` OPENED — THE LARGEST REALM ON WPT, 7,538/96,682 → 94,468/96,682 (7.8% → 97.7%), all 43 files improved, ZERO regressions):**
Took the pointer the previous two arcs had banked and then declined twice. `editing` is **116,600 subtests, the largest realm on all of WPT, with zero ledger rows**, and our entire answer was `execCommand() { return false; }` — one line. `queryCommandEnabled`, `queryCommandIndeterm`, `queryCommandState`, `queryCommandSupported` and `queryCommandValue` **did not exist at all**, so feature detection could not even discover the feature was missing. This is what every comment box, CMS, webmail composer and school assignment form on the web runs on, and it is exactly the older, cheaper, less-maintained sites — the ones reachable from a hand-me-down laptop — that have no fallback for it.
**#514 the commanded verdict** could not start until a root cause underneath the realm was fixed. ⭐⭐⭐ **`getComputedStyle(anything).display` answered `block` — for EVERY element on EVERY page.** The editing spec's first predicate is "is this a block node", and told `block` about a `<span>`, a `<b>`, an `<a>` and a `<sub>`, **there were no inline nodes anywhere in any document** and not one algorithm below could have worked. The cause was one table entry: `_GCS_DEFAULTS.display = 'block'` was being used as CSS's *initial* value, but CSS's initial `display` is **`inline`** — `block` is a **UA STYLESHEET RULE**. *A defaults table is not a stylesheet.* The same gap made `<b>` compute `font-weight: 400`, `<i>` compute `font-style: normal` and `<u>` compute `text-decoration: none` — **an element whose entire purpose is to carry one declaration reported that it did not carry it** — and made `<font color=red>` compute black, so the engine could not read back formatting it had written one line earlier. So: a real UA stylesheet (HTML §15, as a *table* of bare type selectors — one map lookup, the selector engine never involved), wired in at an origin **below presentational hints and below every author rule**; plus `<font color>`/`<font face>`/`align`/`bgcolor` hints, which needed HTML's **"rules for parsing a legacy colour value"** (`chucknorris` really is `rgb(192,0,0)`; the algorithm rejects exactly two things, because *a typo should cost you a hue, not the page*). Then the editing engine's foundation and **every READ path**: 7,538 → **77,803**. That order was deliberate — two-thirds of what these tests assert is what the engine *believes* about a document it has not touched, and **an engine that cannot read formatting correctly cannot possibly write it.**
**#515 the styled verdict** made the twelve inline commands write. They all funnel into one algorithm — *set the selection's value* — whose four steps each prevent a specific kind of rot: **clear**, **push down**, **force**, **reorder**. ⭐⭐ Skip *push down* and **un-bolding one word silently un-bolds the whole paragraph**; skip the merge in *force* and every keystroke adds another `<span>`, which is the classic "why is this email 2 MB" bug and, on a metered connection, somebody's money. ⭐⭐ **The DOM's range mutation rules are wrong for an editor on purpose** — they move boundary points *out of the way* of a move, which is right for an observer and exactly wrong for a caret, so every move goes through `_edMovePreservingRanges`. ⭐⭐ **An override is the memory of a formatting choice made with nothing selected** — press Bold with a bare caret and type — and it must die the instant the caret moves. → **82,962**.
**#516 the typed verdict** did the half a person actually operates: **nobody clicks the bold button as often as they press Enter.** `deleteSelection`, whitespace canonicalization, `fixDisallowedAncestors`, indent/outdent, list toggling, justification, autolinking, and every insertion and deletion command. ⭐⭐⭐ **A `<br>` at the very end of a block draws NOTHING** — the line it would start does not exist yet — which is why every editor emits *two* for one Enter, and the check is answered by **measuring** (`offsetHeight`), only possible because quest #505 made layout real. ⭐⭐ **Deletion is a MERGE, not a removal**, which is why it is the longest algorithm in the spec and why every insertion command begins by calling it. ⭐⭐ `fixDisallowedAncestors` **is what stops a document changing shape every time it is saved** — an element HTML does not allow serializes to one thing and re-parses as another. → **94,468/96,682**, with `createlink` 441/441, `inserthorizontalrule` 1347/1348, `justifyleft` 2500/2503, `outdent` 2540/2550, `removeformat` 1831/1832.
**⚠️⚠️ A HARNESS FIND THAT NEARLY PUBLISHED A FAKE TABLE.** The first #516 probe pass came back with **all 43 files at exactly their pre-arc baselines** — from a binary that scored `bold.html` 3022/3048 by hand thirty seconds later. Six `obscura-pre` servers from the previous ritual pass had been **orphaned onto ports 9400–9405**; the new run's servers each exited with *"Address already in use"*, and the runner's ready-check `curl` then **succeeded against the stale server**. ⭐⭐⭐ **A STALE SERVER ON THE PORT DOES NOT ERROR — IT PRODUCES A COMPLETE, PLAUSIBLE, ENTIRELY WRONG TABLE.** That is the same shape as this campaign's recurring engine lesson, relocated into the harness: *a ready-check that only asks "is something answering on this port" is not a ready-check.* `scripts/wpt_batch_par.sh` now has a pre-flight port refusal **and** a per-chunk `kill -0` on the server PID, so a server that died on bind is FATAL rather than silently substituted.
**⚠️ ZERO REGRESSIONS, THE STRONG PROOF: the 199-file ritual run against the PRE-ARC binary and the new one, diffed PER FILE — 198 of 199 rows identical.** The one moved row (`naturalWidth-naturalHeight-width-height` 210 → 188) is the file the memory already flags as flaky under batch load; re-measured on **fresh servers** the pre-arc binary scores **189/258** and the new one **210/258** — not a regression but an **improvement of 21**, caught by the batch in opposite directions. Which is exactly why a moved row is investigated and not reverted.

Making it incremental is worth ~600 subtests in this realm alone.

**Session 2026-08-08 (Quests #511–#513 — the decoded, loaded & sourced arc: THE IMAGE DECODER, 233-file probe 189/1036 → 601/1036, 76 files improved, ZERO regressions):**

Five WPT ImageBitmap files scored nothing because their shared helper awaits a video; **a promise that never settles does not fail one thing, it stops everything behind it.** Media elements now fail resource selection out loud, which is also what lets a real player show its poster instead of a spinner that never stops.
**#513 the sourced verdict** is the most on-mission piece of the arc: **`srcset`, `sizes` and `<picture>`** — how a page offers a small file to a small device, and we were declining to ask for it. All three HTML algorithms, plus **SVG natural dimensions read straight out of the file** (CSS Images' default sizing algorithm against 300×150 — no rasterizer needed, the size is written down) and **density correction**. `update-the-source-set` **0/89 → 88/89**; `naturalWidth-naturalHeight-width-height` **0/258 → 206/258**. ⭐⭐⭐ **Choosing the SMALLEST sufficient density is the entire point** — on a 1× screen, fetching the 3× file spends nine times the bytes to draw the same pixels, and "pick the last one" is the same single line of code. ⭐⭐ **Zero is a value, negative is an absence**: `width="0"` means zero pixels wide, `width="-5"` means use the default 300, and eighteen subtests move in opposite directions on that one distinction.

Chose the region under the **standing order** by re-surveying the whole platform against a fresh Chrome run summary and diffing every realm against the ledger. Four realms sat at **zero ledger rows**: `editing` (116,600 subtests — the largest realm on all of WPT), `content-security-policy` (4,354), `mathml` (3,472) and `html/canvas` (5,733). `editing` was **deliberately passed over and banked as the next pointer** — it is a layout- and selection-bound swamp that could eat three quests and show little. `html/canvas` was taken because reading the code showed it was not *missing*: **it was lying.** `fill()`, `stroke()`, `clip()`, `closePath()`, `bezierCurveTo()` and **every single transform method** were empty functions; `rect()` filled immediately instead of adding to the path; `fillText` painted **pseudo-random noise from the fingerprint PRNG**; the bitmap was **born full of per-pixel noise** where the spec says transparent black; `toDataURL()` returned a hand-assembled base64 string with a PNG signature and **no image behind it**.
